channel.title: Clisa Geopolitics
channel.description: A geopolitical dashboard analyzing Northeast Asian security, great-power competition, and conflicts in Europe and the Middle East from South Korea’s vantage point. Each issue comes with a situation assessment, a strategy evaluation, what it means for people, and probabilistic forecasts.

item.title: Forecast review · November 23 · 6 revised, 6 unchanged
item.description: Clisa Geopolitics adjusted six forecasts and left six unchanged. It lowered the Second Thomas Shoal forecast as the deadline nears with no report of a blocked resupply, and lowered the probability of a Polish Article 4 request after Poland chose to seek reinforcement of NATO's surveillance mission instead following the latest missile incident. It raised the forecast that Brent will end the year below $90 as prices fell close to that threshold.

item.title: Features · Previewing the Miami G20: a truce that will hold, chip controls that won't ease
item.description: The seventh feature, “Previewing the Miami G20: a truce that will hold, chip controls that won’t ease,” is now up. Drawing on 72 AI-run negotiations among each country’s decision-makers, it looks at how events are likely to unfold around the December G20 summit in Miami and the January 10 expiry of the U.S.-China trade truce, and sets out the dated signals that will show them coming.

item.title: Features · Trump's last two years: a president in a hurry, strongmen who can wait
item.description: The sixth feature, “Trump’s last two years: a president in a hurry, strongmen who can wait,” is now up. It looks at how Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong Un are likely to respond as President Trump, having lost Congress, rushes to secure foreign-policy wins in his last two years, and at how the cost of such deals could fall on allies such as South Korea.

item.title: Forecast review · November 16 · 6 revised, 6 unchanged
item.description: Clisa Geopolitics lowered six forecasts and kept six unchanged, reflecting the absence of any move toward a ceasefire or the lifting of the blockade since the U.S. president said no deal with Iran was needed and the blockade was widened, the fall in European gas prices since late October, and the approach of a deadline with no reported blocking of Philippine resupply missions.

item.title: Method change · Strategic actors for the Russia-Ukraine War issue changed to Germany and the United States
item.description: The strategic actors for the Russia-Ukraine War issue are now Germany and the United States, replacing Ukraine. The change was made to assess the choices of the countries that can alter the outcome of this war. The assessment based on the Ukrainian government's goals has been kept as a "party analysis" rather than removed, and the forecasts and their resolution records are unchanged.

item.title: Method change · Industry Outlook page discontinued
item.description: Industry Outlook, the operating-profit outlook for 19 South Korean and U.S. industries, has been taken down. The change was made to focus assessments on how the five conflicts affect people’s incomes and daily lives in each country. People’s Lives continues to show how these conflicts change incomes.

item.title: Forecast review · November 11 · 9 revised
item.description: Clisa Geopolitics has returned two U.S.-China forecasts, raised on November 10, to their earlier probabilities and has raised one related forecast. The November 9 notice from China's Commerce Ministry implemented an extension to January 10, 2027, that was already known when the two forecasts were written, so it was not grounds for raising the probability of a further extension. It also lowered the forecast that the U.S. will resume strikes on mainland Iran from 63 percent to 45 percent, reflecting the secretary of state's statement that economic pressure is an alternative to strikes. It also lowered five forecasts, either because their deadlines are approaching with no new signals or because new polls or announcements have come out.
